summary: At 2026-08-28T14:12:00Z consumer_lag_records spiked to 140,000 records while msg_process_time_ms and partner_webhook_latency_ms both showed large spikes, and consumed_records_sec dropped sharply. Correlation analysis over the 14:00‑14:12 window shows a very strong positive link between msg_process_time_ms and partner_webhook_latency_ms and strong negative links between those latencies and the consumption rate.

evidence.interpretation: Consumer lag records surged to 140k, far above the baseline mean of 45.
Message processing time spiked to 310 ms, well beyond the baseline mean of ~0.93 ms.
Partner webhook latency rose to 305 ms, indicating a sudden slowdown.
Consumed records per second fell to 8, a sharp drop from the baseline mean of 1,230.
Processing time and webhook latency are almost perfectly positively correlated (r≈0.99997).
Consumption rate and webhook latency show a strong negative correlation (r≈-0.99).
Processing time and consumption rate are strongly negatively correlated (r≈-0.99).
